overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: fewer than a quorum discussed the warrant issue privately, and the unlisted topic was unanticipated when the notice was posted, though the AG urged postponing controversial unnoticed topics.

allegations.summary: Four committee members allegedly privately discussed a warrant-signing dispute before the October 16 meeting, outside a posted meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Because less than a quorum discussed the warrant issue outside of a meeting, we decline to find a violation.

allegations.summary: A motion to remove the warrant signer was allegedly voted on under a 'Bills and Payroll' notice that did not indicate a vote was possible.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, we find no violation for this omission.

allegations.summary: The committee allegedly discussed and acted on a topic not listed on the October 16 notice.
allegations.key_passage: Thus, the Committee was permitted to proceed with its discussion of the topic as the chair did not anticipate this discussion at the time that the notice was posted at least 48 hours in advance of the meeting.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
